dimensions.reasons: Group B csa_booth.png and Group A cam_submitted.png clearly establish the intended CSA exhibition-wall composition: red Canada pillar at left, branded screen in the center, pale technical walling, a gray right-side feature, white floor, and dark lit ceiling.
issues: The crucial right-side feature does not convincingly reproduce the reference's large mechanical hatch showing a dark lunar landscape and rover; it reads instead as a pale frosted inset in a generic gray housing.
The central and right wall panels are substantially simpler than the reference's layered angular sci-fi hull construction.
The presentation is cleaner and more like a small CG set than the specific real exhibition-booth environment in the reference.

dimensions.reasons: Across Group A wide_left.png and wide_right.png, the pillar, wall modules, gray hatch structure, and tiled floor are consistently aligned and grounded. The screen is visibly mounted with a projecting frame, and the riveted hatch trim appears attached to its housing.
issues: The long linear light strip above the booth visibly extends beyond the wall with no evident mounting or support, particularly in Group B csa_booth.png.
The dark enclosing backdrop and ceiling read more as an isolated room/set than a clearly resolved open exhibition venue.

dimensions.reasons: The submitted views clearly distinguish the glossy red Canada pillar, blue CSA-branded display, pale-gray wall panels, black ceiling, and white floor. Group A detail_pillar_screen.png shows a legible agency seal and the pillar's white emblem/star language is recognizable.
issues: The screen differs noticeably from the reference's glossy black display and its logo treatment; the submitted blue face and pink emblem do not closely match the target branding presentation.
The right gray structure has a featureless cabinet-like silhouette around most of its surface rather than reading strongly as metallic capsule hull paneling.
The hatch image is low contrast and abstract, with no independently recognizable rover or lunar terrain.

dimensions.reasons: Group B csa_booth.png is cleanly rendered, free of obvious noise, and has coherent shadows, bevels, and lighting. The booth elements have consistent CG construction and remain readable from several Group A angles.
issues: Materials and form language remain overly smooth and simplified, reducing the impression of a fabricated exhibition installation.
The very bright frosted hatch insert is washed out, so its intended imagery cannot be read.
The repeated small floor tiles and pristine surfaces look more synthetic than the broad, real exhibition floor panels and varied finishes of the reference.

dimensions.reasons: Group A cam_submitted.png and wide_right.png preserve the main left-to-right arrangement well: red freestanding Canada panel, central screen wall, a vertical divider, then the large gray hatch-side structure. The white floor and overhead dark ceiling/lighting are also correctly situated relative to the wall.
issues: The right-side mechanical feature is narrower and more isolated from the central wall than the broader, integrated hull-panel composition in the reference.
The reference's diagonal-stripe motif and multiple layered wall zones near the hatch are largely absent.

dimensions.reasons: The wall, tall pillar, screen, and floor have broadly plausible exhibition-booth proportions in Group B csa_booth.png, and none of the main visible structures appears miniature or physically impossible.
issues: The central screen appears comparatively small for its large surrounding panel compared with the prominent display in the reference.
The hatch inset is undersized and too vertically narrow to carry the visual weight of the reference's large mechanical portal.
The dense small brick-like floor tiling gives a less convincing scale than the reference's large floor panels.

dimensions.reasons: Group B csa_booth.png provides a coherent cool high-tech lighting scheme: dark ceiling, bright edge strips, surface-mounted square lights, soft wall illumination, and a clearly differentiated glossy red panel. The floor reads as pale and mostly matte.
issues: The gray wall/hull surfaces do not visibly convey brushed matte metal; they primarily read as smooth light-gray painted CG material.
The screen does not strongly read as emissive or glossy in the way the target display does.
Over-bright lighting on the inset hatch makes its intended lunar display unreadable rather than keeping the hatch clear.

dimensions.reasons: The main booth modules requested are present: Canada pillar with emblems and wordmark, agency screen, white floor, dark ceiling with floodlights/strip lights, and a riveted right-side framed inset. These are visible in Group A cam_submitted.png and Group B csa_booth.png.
issues: No clear lunar surface or rover is visible through the right-side hatch in any submitted view.
The required hull-panel seams, stiffeners, and layered mechanical detailing are much less developed than in the target.
The reference's distinctive angular inset trim, dark upper hatch opening, lower rover display, and diagonal stripe wall motif are missing or reduced to minimal generic rails.

criteria.criterion: The booth is a coherent human-scale CSA capsule environment with the required three-zone organization, proportions, depth, and circulation logic.
The red pillar is complete in form, branding, side placement, and satin-lacquer finish.
criteria.evidence: The left side of csa_booth.png clearly shows a full-height red freestanding pillar with a white maple-leaf-like emblem at the top, two white four-pointed star emblems, and a readable white “Canada” wordmark near its base. Broad soft highlights on the red surface show a smooth lacquered sheen distinct from the matte gray wall and floor.

criteria.criterion: The central display is correctly mounted, branded, self-lit, and visibly produces localized screen glow.
The opposing wall is a complete brushed-matte metallic spacecraft hull system with all specified visible structural-detail classes and reference construction language.
The prominent hatch is an integrated hull opening that reveals a recognizable lunar surface and rover at spatial depth.
criteria.evidence: The right-side feature in cam_submitted.png and wide_left.png is a riveted, rounded-rectangle frosted inset with horizontal bars, but its pale interior only shows indistinct circular patterns. No recognizable rover or clearly lunar rocky/cratered terrain is visible, so the opening does not convincingly reveal a spatial exterior lunar scene.

criteria.criterion: The overhead system is a dark suspended ceiling fitted with surface-mounted floodlights and visible edge light strips.
The booth floor is visibly white, spatially continuous beneath the stand, and matte rather than glossy.
criteria.evidence: csa_booth.png and preview.png show a continuous light-white tiled floor extending broadly beneath and well in front of the booth. Its tile seams are visible and it has only subdued diffuse lighting, without mirror-like reflections.

criteria.criterion: Native area lighting, screen glow, differentiated materials, and staging combine into a cool high-tech image that preserves hull and hatch clarity.
The active author camera is slightly off-front and its final composition clearly communicates every principal booth zone.
The actual author final image is delivered as an openable high-resolution PNG.
The native Blender project is openable, complete, editable, configured for Cycles, and corresponds to the delivered final PNG.

notes: The booth is recognizably a Canadian Space Agency exhibition concept with a strong broad layout and clean rendering. Its principal reconstruction weakness is the right-side capsule/hatch: although a riveted framed inset exists, its washed-out frosted panel does not show the requested lunar rover scene and the surrounding hull lacks the target's mechanical specificity.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
